The offering is read on the dashboard (outline 'Only workspace admins are offered the sidebar entry', row Priya | the dashboard | offered), but the follow outline 'A workspace admin reaches the workspace integrations from the sidebar' has Examples 'Identity Platform's board', 'Identity Platform's integrations page' and 'a new Slack route on Identity Platform' only: no scenario follows the entry from the dashboard. Coverage is adequate by composition (the dashboard row asserts href == /workspace/integrations and that address is followed three times), so no promise is left without a falsifier, but the note claims more than the cited rows show.
findings.remediation: Either add one Examples row 'the dashboard' to 'A workspace admin reaches the workspace integrations from the sidebar' in integrations-wayfinding.feature, which removes the residue outright, or reword the comment to say that the dashboard entry's address is read there and that same address is followed from the other pages.

The offering half keeps a falsifier at the migration target: integrations-wayfinding.feature outline 'Only workspace admins are offered the sidebar entry' holds the row (Priya, the dashboard, offered), and support/integrations_wayfinding.rs then_sidebar_offered (:417-439) asserts the page sidebar is non-empty (a precondition, so a blind reading fails loudly), then that exactly one sidebar link reads 'Integrations' and its href equals /workspace/integrations. The reachability half holds by composition, not by one scenario: the dashboard row asserts the entry's address is /workspace/integrations, and outline 'A workspace admin reaches the workspace integrations from the sidebar' follows that same sidebar address (support/integrations_wayfinding.rs when_follow_sidebar :398-414) from a board, the integrations page and a new-route form and asserts she lands on the workspace integrations page. The slice oracle itself keeps both arms of the gate the retired Priya row touched: crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/nav-quick-actions.feature asserts the user menu contains a link to /workspace/integrations for the workspace admin and for the two-admin row, and does not contain it for the plain member and the instance-only admin. L2's workspace-admin case keeps a falsifier inside the reviewed oracle, independently of eip-06.

No leak falsifier is lost. The surviving dashboard rows (Lena, Sam, Marco 'not offered') run through then_link_offered's negative arm (support/external_integration_plugins.rs:3896-3907), which counts all_link_hrefs (:3845, no in_sidebar filter), so a rail entry leaked to a non-admin still fails there; integrations-wayfinding's sidebar negatives cover the same leak with a positive control. The asymmetry that the page-wide reading has no positive row of its own predates this delta: the 'offered' arm always counted the body-only link_hrefs, so the retirement removed no positive control for the page-wide reading.

Retiring is sound against the keep-each-pair-once rule: a row rewritten in eip-06 to read the rail would repeat the stimulus (a workspace admin opens the dashboard) and the assertion (one Integrations entry to /workspace/integrations in the sidebar) that integrations-wayfinding US-IW-01 already owns, and would add no distinct observation. No other oracle still pins the dashboard body as the offering surface; instance-integration-setup.feature:194 follows Integrations on the instance admin dashboard (/admin/instance/workspaces), whose own body carries that link and which this change does not touch.

diagnostic: Delta accepted: retiring the two eip-06 rows is sound and no promise loses its falsifier. The retired rows pinned the dashboard BODY as the offering surface (their reading filters the sidebar out on purpose), so the owner's removal of Quick actions supersedes them rather than relocating them; a rewritten sidebar-reading row in eip-06 would repeat the stimulus and assertion that integrations-wayfinding US-IW-01 already owns and would add no distinct observation. The offering promise keeps a falsifier at the migration target (row Priya | the dashboard | offered, asserting exactly one sidebar entry whose href is /workspace/integrations, behind a non-empty-sidebar precondition, with three not-offered rows as contrast), and the slice oracle independently keeps both arms of the same gate through the user-menu rows. The reachability promise holds by composition: the dashboard row fixes the address and three other scenarios follow that address to the workspace integrations page. The leak falsifier for non-admins survives unchanged, since the remaining dashboard rows read page-wide including the rail. The superseded scope is recorded in the file and in the design rows, not silently deleted. Two non-blocking oracle findings remain, neither invalidating this phase: the migration comment claims integrations-wayfinding follows the entry from the dashboard, which no Examples row does (one added row removes the residue, or reword the note), and the follows-step regex keeps a now-dead 'the dashboard' alternative that could only fail and invites reinstating the superseded promise. Evidence: my own tag selection was terminated (SIGTERM, zero scenarios) to avoid contending with another session's gate in the shared VM; the judgment rests on the host default lane at this exact clean revision (1912 scenarios, 1912 passed), whose stdout records both the retired file's remaining rows and the migration-target rows green. typesafe: unavailable (TYPESAFE_API_KEY absent; a caller-side request defect was repaired first), so every reason here is a reviewer reason checked against the cited bytes. Unobserved residue, unchanged by this delta: no browser-lane observation of the enlarged folded rail (P4 stays a completion obligation), and the page-wide link reading still has no positive control inside eip-06.
